description: Advisories from `composer audit --locked` that this fork knowingly carries.
The gate (scripts/ci/composer-audit.sh) fails on any advisory NOT listed
here. That is the point: none of these versions is this fork's choice —
app/composer.json is upstream's bluespice/core and every affected package is
a transitive dependency of MediaWiki 1.43.9 / BlueSpice 5.1.9, or a vendored
extension of it — so a bare audit would be red on every push and would be
ignored within a week. What is worth failing a push over is a NEW advisory,
and that is what this comparison detects.
Entries marked ACTION REQUIRED are fixable, but only by re-vendoring an
upstream tree, which is docs/dev/upgrade-runbook.md, not a PR. Read them
at the start of every upgrade: they are the reason to take one.
This file cannot see: MediaWiki core (vendored source, not a composer
package — that is the release-watch job, Track B), the two frozen packages
(stripped from composer.lock — Track C, see VERSIONS.yml and SECURITY.md),
or any vendored extension that is not also a composer package.

guzzlehttp/guzzle.why: Pinned to exactly 7.12.3 by upstream's app/composer.json (bluespice/core); wikimedia/shellbox asks for ^7.9.2. The 1.43.9 / 5.1.9 upgrade cleared six of the ten advisories this package used to carry — these four survive because they are fixed in 7.14.2 and 7.15.1, past the version upstream pins. All four are medium and none has a CVE: URI fragments disclosed in redirect Referer headers, host-only cookie scope not preserved, unbounded response cookies, and Proxy-Authorization headers forwarded to origin servers. Guzzle is used server-side by shellbox, monolog and the OAuth path against configured hosts; no untrusted URL reaches it from wiki content, so the redirect- and cookie-scoped issues need an attacker who already controls an outbound target. Moves when upstream repins.

mediawiki/maps.why: ACTION REQUIRED, and still open after the 1.43.9 / 5.1.9 upgrade, which did not move Maps. CVE-2026-52854 (high) is stored XSS through the `overlays` parameter of the display_map parser function, fixed in 12.1.3; this tree vendors 11.0.1 at app/extensions/Maps and the composer entry follows that vendored tree. Any editor who can save wikitext can reach the parser function, which makes this the most exposed entry in this file — it is the only high left and the only one reachable from wiki content. Fixing it means re-vendoring the Maps extension, an upstream-tree change (docs/dev/upgrade-runbook.md), not a lockfile edit or a CI-gate change. Recorded here so it cannot be forgotten.

web-auth/webauthn-lib.why: Low, and specific to SimpleFakeCredentialGenerator used with an empty secret — a username-enumeration hardening feature, not an authentication bypass. The upgrade moved this 4.9.2 → 4.9.3, which does not clear it: the advisory covers >=4.9.0,<5.3.5 and mediawiki/web-authn requires ^4.9.2, so the fix is a major bump upstream has not taken. Not this fork's version to choose.
